sentence: نْحَبّ نِشْرِي voiture جْدِيدَة هَا الْعَام
raw: نحب نشري voiture جديدة ها العام
ipa: ˈnħabb ˈniʃriː vwaˈtir ˈʒdiːda ˈhaː ˈlʕaːm
gloss_en: I want to buy a new car this year
notes: [fr-cs] voiture 'car' → [vwaˈtir]: Fr /y/→[i], uvular /ʁ/→native /r/, /v/ retained (deep Algiers French adstrate; boucherit2002). PIPELINE WRONG (en-GB donor default): 'fuitjuːr'. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: my mobile phone doesn't work well
notes: [fr-cs] portable 'mobile' → [pərˈtabl]: /p/ retained (adstrate), pretonic /ɔ/→[ə] (Algiers reduces short vowels to [ə]/∅ in weak positions (Boucherit 2002 heavy syncope)), /ʁ/→[r]. PIPELINE WRONG (en donor): 'buːrtabl' (/p/→[b]). table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: there is a big problem at work
notes: [fr-cs] problème → [prəbˈlɛm]: /p/ retained, /ʁ/→[r], pretonic vowel→[ə] (Algiers reduces short vowels to [ə]/∅ in weak positions (Boucherit 2002 heavy syncope)). كاين 'there is' (Algiers). PIPELINE WRONG (en donor): 'brublm'. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: I paid the electricity bill yesterday
notes: [fr-cs] facture 'bill' → [fakˈtura]: syllabic /ʁ/ resolved with epenthetic [a] (holes2004). genitive exponent تاع (Algiers). PIPELINE WRONG (en donor): 'faktjuːr'. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: I have an appointment with the doctor tomorrow
notes: [fr-cs] rendez-vous 'appointment' → [rɑndiˈvu]: nasal /ɑ̃/→[ɑn], /v/ retained. PIPELINE WRONG (en donor): 'rindizfaws' (reads the digraph as English). table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

sentence: هَادَا شِي normal مَا تْخَمِّمْش بْزَّاف
raw: هادا شي normal ما تخممش بزاف
ipa: ˈhaːdaː ˈʃiː nərˈmal ˈmaː txaˈmmimʃ ˈbzzaːf
gloss_en: this is normal, don't think too much
notes: [fr-cs] normal → [nərˈmal]: pretonic /ɔ/→[ə] (Algiers reduces short vowels to [ə]/∅ in weak positions (Boucherit 2002 heavy syncope)), /ʁ/→[r]. PIPELINE WRONG (en donor): 'nuːrmal'. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: give me a pen to write with
notes: [fr-cs] stylo 'pen' → [stiˈlu]: Fr /y/→[i], /o/→[u]; well-integrated Algiers loan (the pipeline's 'stilu' happens close but is en-donor and mis-stressed). table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: thank you very much for the help
notes: [fr-cs] merci 'thanks' → [mərˈsi]: pretonic /ɛ/→[ə] (Algiers reduces short vowels to [ə]/∅ in weak positions (Boucherit 2002 heavy syncope)), /ʁ/→[r]. PIPELINE WRONG (en donor): 'marsi' (full [a]). table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

sentence: نْشُوفَك فِي weekend إِنْ شَاءَ الله
raw: نشوفك في weekend إن شاء الله
ipa: ˈnʃuːfak ˈfiː wiːkind ˈʔin ˈʃaːʔa ˈallah
gloss_en: we'll see you on the weekend, God willing
notes: [en-cs] weekend→wiːkind. English is the minority CS donor in Algiers; French dominates. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

sentence: عَنْدِي laptop جْدِيد أَمَّا wifi بَطِيء
raw: عندي laptop جديد أما wifi بطيء
ipa: ˈʕandiː labtub ˈʒdiːd ˈʔammaː wifi bɑˈtˤiːʔ
gloss_en: I have a new laptop but the wifi is slow
notes: [en-cs] laptop→labtub (/p/→[b]); wifi→wifi. NOTE: Algiers reduces short vowels to [ə]/∅ in weak positions (Boucherit 2002 heavy syncope), so a fast Algiers reading has [ʔamma], [labtəb] — the pipeline emits the full-vowel form here (documented divergence, kept pinned as engine truth). table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: send me the email about the meeting
notes: [en-cs] email→imel; meeting→miːtinɡ (/ŋ/→[nɡ]). genitive exponent تاع (Algiers). table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: I buy everything online a lot
notes: [en-cs] online→unlin. بزّاف 'a lot' (Algiers hallmark). table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: I have a new telephone at home
notes: [loan] loan تلفون (< Fr téléphone) → [tiliˈfuːn], attested Algiers form (boucherit2002). Pipeline reads the vocalised loan natively and matches. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: I went to Oran by bus yesterday
notes: [loan] loan كار (< Fr/It car 'coach') → [kaːr]: Algiers has NO imāla, so the long /aː/ keeps its back quality (boucherit2002) — the isogloss against Tunis [kɛːr]. Pipeline matches. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: give me the fork so I can eat
notes: [loan] loan فرشيطة (< Fr fourchette 'fork') → [farˈʃiːtˤɑ], attested Algiers household loan; ط emphatic backs the vowel to [ɑ] (boucherit2002). Pipeline matches. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: I took my grandfather to the hospital yesterday
notes: [loan] loan سبيطار (< Fr/It (h)ospital) → [sbiːˈtˤɑːr], attested Algiers form; emphatic backing [ɑː]. STRESS ARTIFACT (documented, kept as engine truth): pipeline emits 'sbiˈːtˤɑːr' with the stress mark inside the length mark — cf. the ar-EG rows. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

sentence: نِمْشِي لِلْبِيرُو كُلّ صْبَاح فِي الْعَاصِمَة
raw: نمشي للبيرو كل صباح في العاصمة
ipa: ˈnimʃiː lilˈbiːruː ˈkull ˈsˤbaːħ ˈfiː ˈlʕɑːsˤima
gloss_en: I go to the office every morning in the capital
notes: [loan] loan بيرو (< Fr bureau 'office/desk') → [biːru], everyday Algiers loan (boucherit2002); ع pharyngeal + emphatic ص back /a/ in العاصمة→[lʕɑːsˤima]. Pipeline matches. table: default pan-Arabic (Watson 2002; Holes 2004)

gloss_en: how are you? are you well?
notes: [arabizi] Arabizi (Algiers 3arabi). Spells وَاش رَاك؟ رَاك مْلِيح (Algiers greeting; boucherit2002 attests rāk, mlīḥ 'well'). No Arabizi path in the pipeline; ipa hand-derived as the Algiers reading — no imāla, /aː/ stays back. table: n/a

gloss_en: where did you go yesterday?
notes: [arabizi] Arabizi: 7=ح. Spells وِين رُحْت الْبَارِح. ipa hand-derived; بارِح keeps back [baːriħ] (no Algiers imāla; boucherit2002). table: n/a

gloss_en: please call me before you come
notes: [arabizi] Arabizi: 3=ع, 9=ق, T=ط. Spells يَعَيْشِك عَيَّطْلِي قَبْل مَا تْجِي. ipa hand-derived; Algiers keeps the /aj/ of يعيشك as [aj] (jaˈʕajʃik) — NO Tunis ay→iː monophthong here, the two Maghrebi leaves diverge — and قبل reduces to [qbəl] by heavy syncope (Algiers reduces short vowels to [ə]/∅ in weak positions (Boucherit 2002 heavy syncope)). table: n/a
